statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the cardinality of the set { T(words[i]) | 0 <= i < len(words) }, where T(w) is the concatenation of the standard Morse codes of the letters of w (the 26-letter table: a='.-', b='-...', c='-.-.', d='-..', e='.', f='..-.', g='--.', h='....', i='..', j='.---', k='-.-', l='.-..', m='--', n='-.', o='---', p='.--.', q='--.-', r='.-.', s='...', t='-', u='..-', v='...-', w='.--', x='-..-', y='-.--', z='--..'). Equivalently, if M is the 26-element array ['.-','-...','-.-.','-..','.','..-.','--.','....','..','.---','-.-','.-..','--','-.','---','.--.','--.-','.-.','...','-','..-','...-','.--','-..-','-.--','--..'] indexed from 0 for 'a' to 25 for 'z', then T(w) = M[w[0]-97] concatenated with M[w[1]-97] concatenated ... with M[w[len(w)-1]-97].
preconditions: len(words) >= 1 and len(words) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 12; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words) and every j with 0 <= j < len(words[i]), 97 <= words[i][j] <= 122 (the byte is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z').
